name: Intent registry
scoped_purpose: Use for recording every problem, solution, implementation, ideal and metric of a repository as linked records that people and checks both read. Avoids holding results (those belong to the results log) and avoids prose design documents.
goals: Every intent item is one record with every template field filled; every link resolves both ways; every file reaches a solution through the ownership map.
knowledge: The intent template in the evolvable-structure skill; Joshua's Project Documentation board (solution definitions apart from implementations); requirements traceability practice.
measures_of_success: A reader can follow any file to its problem and ideal, and every record is complete.
inputs: Hand-edited records of each type, the ownership map.
outputs: A linked intent network that the check, the tracker and the selection read.
usage_notes: Add or edit a record before building a new capability; the check names anything missing.

name: Template sync
scoped_purpose: Use for deriving the registry's fields from the intent template in the skill, so the author's wording is the only definition. Avoids adding fields of its own or interpreting the template.
goals: The registry's fields equal the template's fields after every refinement.
knowledge: The skill's `SKILL.md` as the source of truth; derived-copy practice already used for the standing instructions.
measures_of_success: A template refinement shows up as named missing fields on the next check, with no hand edit of any schema.
outputs: A committed field list per type.
effects: Fails the check when the committed field list is stale.
usage_notes: Run after Joshua edits the template; public CI, which cannot read the skill, checks records against the committed list.

name: Ownership map
scoped_purpose: Use for assigning every file to exactly one component and every component to the solutions it serves. Avoids describing what the code does (the solution records do that).
goals: No file unowned, no component serving nothing, no module past the size ceiling, imports pointing inward.
knowledge: Layered and hexagonal architecture; code owners practice; the repository's split rule.
measures_of_success: Code that serves no solution is found and removed.
inputs: The file tree and the component records.
outputs: File-to-solution links and the generated component index.
usage_notes: A new file joins a component in the same change; a file that fits no solution is a sign the code should go.

name: Implementation selection
scoped_purpose: Use for choosing which implementation serves a swappable solution by name, configuration or table default. Avoids deciding which one is best (the leaderboard does) and avoids per-call branching.
goals: Switching is a data change; an unknown name fails with the choices; every listed implementation loads.
knowledge: Ports and adapters; plugin registries; lazy loading of optional dependencies.
measures_of_success: Every switch works from configuration alone and no typo falls back silently.
parameters: Solution id, implementation name, configuration overrides.
outputs: The chosen implementation's class and its configuration type.
usage_notes: Every solution with a port has a table entry whose default equals the measured winner or a declared tie.

name: Measurement harness
scoped_purpose: Use for running each implementation of a solution against that solution's cases through the live code and recording the result with its provenance. Avoids ranking and avoids tests that only check code runs.
goals: Every eval solution has cases, a scorer and implementations that drive shipped code; every recorded result carries its commit, case hash, cost and tokens; a call budget stops a run.
knowledge: Evaluation practice for language models (held-out cases, staged sample sizes, judged rubrics); experiment tracking; the eval ladder of three, ten and thirty cases.
measures_of_success: Any result can be rerun from its record, and no result was produced by code other than what ships.
parameters: Solution, implementation, case subset, call budget.
inputs: Case files, the implementation, any live services the cases need.
effects: Model spend on live runs; refuses to run against production.
usage_notes: Start live runs small and stop at the budget; re-record on committed code after any change to measured code or cases.

name: Leaderboard
scoped_purpose: Use for deciding, from recorded results, which implementation of a solution is best or whether they tie. Avoids running anything and avoids comparing results from different case sets.
goals: A win is called only outside the noise margin; ties, losses and unmeasured arms are labelled as such; comparison-only arms are never rivals.
knowledge: Statistical noise in small judged samples; cost and token accounting; Pareto comparison of quality and cost.
measures_of_success: Its verdicts match known rankings on pinned cases and never call a tie a win.
parameters: Noise margin and spend tolerance per component.
outputs: A verdict per solution and a ranked board.
usage_notes: The check requires the selected implementation to be the winner or a declared tie with a reason.

name: Discriminating cases
scoped_purpose: Use for proving that a solution's cases can tell a sound implementation from a naive one, especially for rules where best cannot vary. Avoids inventing rivals that exist only to lose a comparison.
goals: Every invariant solution has at least one naive baseline that fails its cases.
knowledge: Mutation testing; the gap between a passing test and a meaningful one.
measures_of_success: No case set passes everything that is put in front of it.
inputs: A solution's cases and its naive baselines.
outputs: A pass or fail per baseline.
usage_notes: Write the naive version a first draft would produce, not a deliberately silly one.

name: Structure check
scoped_purpose: Use for enforcing every structural rule on each change, before commit and in tests. Avoids judging code quality beyond the rules, and avoids rules no one can fix.
goals: Every rule violation is reported by rule and path; a clean tree passes; strict mode refuses results from uncommitted code; an exception lives only as a waiver with a reason that disappears when it stops applying.
knowledge: Architecture tests and linters; the repository's numbered rules; the leaderboard (reused, not copied).
measures_of_success: Every injected violation is caught, nothing clean is flagged, and it runs fast enough that nobody skips it.
inputs: The repository, the registry, the results log, the waivers.
outputs: A list of violations and an exit code.
effects: Blocks a commit or a test run that breaks a rule.
usage_notes: Add a rule when a mistake has happened twice; delete a rule that stops catching anything.

name: Review tracker
scoped_purpose: Use for putting the whole intent network and its current results in front of a human reviewer, and carrying their edits back. Avoids being a second source of truth for anything but review columns.
goals: Every record and its latest verdict appears in one sheet; reviewer edits survive rebuilds and flow back to the repository.
knowledge: Spreadsheets as the team's review medium; two-way sync keyed by record id.
measures_of_success: Joshua can make and record every review decision from the sheet.
parameters: Which tabs, which columns a reviewer may edit.
inputs: The registry and the results log.
outputs: Generated tracker tables and the synced sheet.
usage_notes: Rebuild after any registry or result change; the check fails when the tracker is stale.

name: Consumer check
scoped_purpose: Use for letting a system built on a library record which library solution each of its parts serves, score its own implementations with the library's cases, and see its version lag. Avoids copying the library's checks into the consumer and avoids putting the consumer's private data in the library.
goals: Every integration point maps to a library solution; every consumer store is scored by the library's cases; the pin's lag is visible.
knowledge: Consumer-driven contract testing; the library's own structure check and cases.
measures_of_success: The consumer passes with nothing unmapped, unscored or unexplained.
parameters: The consumer's registry, root, requirements, solutions and results files; whether lag fails.
usage_notes: Run in the consumer's tests; bump the pin after the library's changes land.

name: The standard
scoped_purpose: Use for teaching anyone, person or AI, how a solution is shaped in this structure and how another repository adopts it. Avoids repeating what the checks already enforce.
goals: One document gives the shape of a solution end to end and the steps to adopt it elsewhere.
knowledge: the adopting repositories as worked examples; the evolvable-structure skill.
measures_of_success: Someone following it alone reaches a passing check.
usage_notes: Read first; update in the same change as any rule.

name: Structure budget
scoped_purpose: Use for keeping the structure's own cost in view and pruning what stops paying. Avoids removing rules that still catch real mistakes.
goals: The effort the structure adds to a change is known, and rules, records and checks that catch nothing are removed.
knowledge: Principle 12 (minimalism) and the skill's difficulties; developer-experience research.
measures_of_success: Small changes stay small and every rule has caught something real.
inputs: The check's history, time per check, files touched per change.
outputs: A periodic report of cost against catches.
usage_notes: Not built yet; this record holds the place so the cost is not forgotten.

name: When metrics are run
scoped_purpose: Use for deciding when each Metric is run, in what stages, with what limit, who approves the spend, and when its result stops counting. Avoids deciding how a metric is implemented or which alternative is best.
goals: Offline metrics run on every change; paid metrics run only when a decision depends on them, in staged samples inside a budget; every recorded result can be told current from stale.
knowledge: Evaluation practice for models (staged and stratified samples, call budgets, noise); continuous integration practice; the cost of re-running against the cost of deciding wrongly.
measures_of_success: Decisions are backed by current results, spend is approved and proportionate, and stale results are found at the change rather than at a release.
